title: A kingdom on the move
paragraphs: Baekje developed within a landscape of rivers, plains, and routes connecting inland settlements to maritime approaches. Political success required more than the capacity to win a battle. A court needed reliable relationships with local leaders, productive lands, and the ability to sustain people who served military or ceremonial roles. The Han River basin was particularly consequential as a corridor linking many of these concerns.

The reign associated with Geunchogo is remembered as an important period of expansion. But stories of expansion are easier to narrate than the daily processes that make expansion durable. Behind military activity stood questions of loyalty, supply, movement, and communication. These create a richer account of why a ruling center could project power beyond its immediate surroundings.
